narrative.overview: A service counter is plain on purpose: the person behind it is there to get something done, not to admire the furniture. This interface works the same way. It sets a calm cool-gray page, one system typeface, a hairline under the header, and leaves everything else (buttons, inputs, selects, tables) to the browser's native controls. The ticket data is the content; the chrome stays out of its way.
keyCharacteristics: Native controls, unstyled; the browser supplies buttons, inputs, selects and tables.
One system font stack, no web fonts, no external origins (SPEC-UI-06).
Cool-gray page, near-black text, one blue reserved for focus.
Flat: no shadows, no radii, one hairline border.

rules.name: The Blue Is Focus Rule
rules.body: Focus Blue appears only as the focus outline. If it shows up as a fill, a link or a heading, it has been misused.

rules.name: The Text-Not-Tint Rule
rules.body: State messages are colored text, not colored panels. Error is bold; success is not.

rules.name: The No-Webfont Rule
rules.body: No font files and no external font requests. The stack must resolve locally.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay flat at rest. Introduce a shadow only if a future overlay genuinely needs separation from the page.

dos: Do keep native controls and add styling only where a state or layout need cannot be met without it.
Do keep the Focus Blue outline on every focusable element (3px, 2px offset).
Do use only the system font stack and same-origin assets.
Do express disabled state with `disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"`, which the spec requires while a request is in flight (SPEC-UI-134).
Do keep copy and labels in Spanish.
donts: Don't load web fonts, icon fonts, CDN scripts or external stylesheets (SPEC-UI-06).
Don't use Focus Blue as a fill, link or decoration color.
Don't add shadows, gradients or rounded decoration to a flat, counter-plain system without an explicit design decision.
Don't put business rules in styling or markup; permissions and transitions belong to the API.
Don't convey state with color alone; pair it with text.
